sources_read: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 53 (#52 task_security_and_secrets), Internal Quality Checks row 53 (E/F annotations: credentials/realistic identities allowed in task.toml/brief, stripped before delivery) and row 15 G (credentials in task data are flagged; only toml allowed), Deterministic Checks A19 check-no-literal-secrets.py
rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (delivery profile, severity table, Known false positives 'Credentials the profile expects')

rules/projects/webdev-task-template (diffed environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/.dockerignore, solution/solve.sh, task.toml)
evidence: Credentials: the only credential-shaped value is task.toml:34 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" (a ${VAR} template, identical to the frozen template block; task.toml differs from rules/projects/webdev-task-template/task.toml only in [task] name/description/keywords and [metadata] lines 5-15). A full-tree regex scan of the frozen task for provider key shapes (sk-, sk-or-, AKIA, ghp_, xox*, AIza, PEM BEGIN ... KEY, JWT eyJ..) returned no hits. The only password is the demo password 'password123' (environment/instructions/walls-and-retention.md:3, tests/app_context.md:8, solution/app/server.js:17), which the workbook (Deterministic A19) and SKILL.md known-false-positives explicitly allow; server.js stores it scrypt-hashed with random salts and issues random session tokens (server.js:51,99,301-303), no secret literal. Dockerfile git identity is turing@local.invalid (reserved TLD). Personal data: seed_data.json (byte-identical in environment/assets and solution/app/seed) has 5 accounts all on the reserved .test TLD (harriet/dev/sian/gwen/paul@kittle.test), a fictional firm 'Kittle & Rowe', fictional matters/targets ('Fenwick Mills'), no phone numbers, addresses, IDs or DOBs; message bodies are mundane synthetic legal chatter. Host paths: grep for drive letters, /Users/, /home/, Documents, turing-workspace, user IDs, AppData returned nothing; every path in brief/notes/prompts is a container path (/app, /assets, /instructions, /app/app.db, /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py). Remote fetch: all URLs are local (http://localhost:3000, http://127.0.0.1:3000 in test.sh:48,136 and prompts) plus the frozen template's https://openrouter.ai/api judge endpoint and the inert text https://example.org/lease (IANA-reserved) inside a message body. Both Dockerfiles, test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py and solve.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template; installs are version-pinned (express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, claude-code@2.1.281, codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7); base images are tag-pinned as the template ships them (template-controlled, not a task defect). The golden app loads only same-origin /styles.css, /app.js, /transcript.css (index.html:7,109; server.js:490) and app.js:14 fetches same-origin paths only; solve.sh only copies files. Injection: no prompt-injection text aimed at the agent or judge (scan for 'ignore previous', 'disregard', 'give full marks', system-prompt markers returned only the checker-not-fixer rule in each prompt.md:8/9). The two markup strings are deliberate, publicly motivated safety fixtures: seed K-16 'Pasted from the lease: Schedule 2 and clause 4, see rent.' (benign tags, no script) and tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:175 criterion safe_formatting which posts ' [click](javascript:alert(9))' to verify escaping; both trace to environment/instructions/conversations.md:13 ('Anything else that looks like markup, scripts or HTML is just text and shows exactly as it was typed...'). They exercise the submission's output escaping with harmless alert() calls only, exfiltrate nothing, and live in grader input rather than as a hidden payload in shipped data, so they are test vectors, not injection payloads in the row-52 sense. Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken app cannot 'pass' this row because the row is a static property of the task bytes; (b) a conforming app that renders the XSS fixture safely is unaffected; an app that executes it only pops an alert inside the judge's sandboxed Chromium against localhost, with no credential in reach (the verifier token is env-templated and not exposed to the app, which runs in a separate environment per task.toml:28). Minor observation (not a row-52 defect, possible row-25 echo of Colderwater lesson 13): safe_formatting asks that https://example.org/lease 'is a link that opens in a new tab'; if the judge clicks it, the tab navigates to a reserved public domain, but the grade depends only on link/new-tab behavior, not on that site's content. Run evidence: none needed for this static row; no full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says so), which does not affect this verdict.
